It uses execSync to run commands, ROT13 obfuscation for the C2 domain, and explicit avoidance of localhost resolution — all consistent with covert data exfiltration/C2 behavior. These actions indicate deliberate malicious intent rather than benign utility.

It also executes system commands via child_process and contacts external IPs (8.8.8.8 and ifconfig.me). The intent (covert data collection and remote exfiltration) is malicious rather than benign.

The setup.py intentionally overrides the installer to gather sensitive system data (whoami, id, uname, hostname, cwd, platform, local IP and public IP) and exfiltrates it to an external host. It runs shell commands via subprocess.check_output, fetches public IP from ifconfig.me, encodes the data, decodes a hardcoded ROT13 domain (ebbgzr.yby -> rootme.lol), leaks chunks via DNS queries (gethostbyname on crafted subdomains) and sends the full payload in an HTTP header — all executed at install time. This is deliberate data-exfiltration/backdoor behavior, not benign, so classify as malware.
Collects IP addresses and contains suspicious URLs, suggesting tracking or targeting capabilities.

The package overrides the install command to run hidden code at install time: it ROT13-decodes obfuscated strings to get "whoami" and a domain ("rootme.lol"), executes that command via subprocess.check_output(shell=True) to capture a local username, hex-encodes the result, performs a DNS lookup for <hex>.<domain> and sends an HTTP request with the hex value in an X-D header. This is covert data exfiltration (sensitive local info sent to an external host), uses obfuscation and suppressed errors to hide behavior, and executes without user consent during installation — clear malicious intent.
